goal: `mc publish` is the one way a step's session or a mend puts a new head on its pull request: it edits only the fields it is given, can retarget the base, publishes a detached HEAD to a named branch, and keeps the description honest by listing the commits that came after it.
Nothing mc tells a session sends it past `mc publish`: the retry preamble, the mend prompt, the pre-tool hook, the toolbox and the help all name it.
`mc merge` refuses an unpushed head or a conflicting pull request at the door, and the merger lands only the head it measured.

Step 2: mc publish writes the description's head as <!-- mc:described <sha> --> (create and body-given edits use the local head); with no body it reads the mark (or the branch's first commit when there is none), and lists the commits after it under ## After the description, editing only the body when that text changes. steps.title: `mc publish --branch <name>` publishes a detached HEAD
steps.done_when: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/publish.test.js` passes with the new tests, and `mc gate` is green.
comments: mc publish --branch <name> publishes a detached HEAD (a mend's worktree). --branch is a strict value; before any network call it refuses (2) when this worktree is on another branch than the name, and when check-ref-format rejects the name. branch becomes flags.branch || current, so the ls-remote and the refusals run on the named branch. A detached HEAD is pushed by pushBranch with detached: true as HEAD:refs/heads/<name>, without -u; the --no-thin retry covers both forms. Without --branch a detached HEAD is still refused on HEAD. Three new tests in tests/mc/publish.test.js; the publish file passes 18/18 and mc gate is GREEN (2672 tests).

For the next reader: an unquoted echo of the pr-edit words is refused by pr-edit, as the pr-create rule already refuses the create words, because the regex cannot tell an echo argument from a command word; a quoted echo passes. mendPrompt says Never `git push`, so the mend test asserts no `git push origin` instead of no push at all.

steps.title: `mc merge` refuses an unpushed head and a conflicting pull request before queueing
steps.done_when: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/merge-command.test.js` passes with the new tests, and `mc gate` is green.
comments: mc merge's door (queueForMerger, src/mc/commands/repo.js) now refuses two things before queueing and before any round is recorded: a pull request GitHub reports mergeable CONFLICTING (gh pr view now asks headRefName,headRefOid,mergeable), and a pull request whose branch the caller's worktree (deps.cwd || process.cwd()) is on at a head origin does not have (ls-remote --heads origin <head> differs from rev-parse HEAD). A failed ls-remote fails open. doorRefusal() is the pure function holding both messages. Tests: tests/mc/merge-command.test.js, describe 'the door refuses what cannot land as asked (ruling 43)'. The merger's landing call (--match-head-commit) is not touched here; that is steps[5].

steps.title: The merger lands only the head it measured: `--match-head-commit`
steps.done_when: `grep -n 'match-head-commit' src/mc/repo-merge.js` finds the landing call, `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/repo-merge.test.js tests/mc/merger.test.js` passes with the new tests, and `mc gate` is green.
comments: Step 6 (--match-head-commit). The squash in repo-merge.js now passes --match-head-commit <sha> to the forge's squash call. The sha is verdict.pr.head_sha for one pull request, or the batch item's head_sha, and it is replaced by the sha freshenBranchForLanding returns when the branch was freshened first. freshenBranchForLanding now returns the full sha as well as the 7-character at. Before the squash, headOnGithub reads headRefOid up to six times, five seconds apart (a sleep dep, defaulting to a timer), and a head that never matches stops the round as drift with a message naming both shas; nothing is merged. With no expected head the landing is unpinned and the round says so. Not covered here: src/mc/docs-merge.js (the --docs form) still squashes without a pin, and the door refusals in success criterion 3 belong to step 4.

Step 6 is built and gate-green on this tree (npm test 2692 tests, 0 failed; repo-merge, merger and repo-freshen suites 113 pass). The landing call in repo-merge.js now pins the squash with --match-head-commit. The expected head is the sha freshenBranchForLanding returns (now also sha, untruncated) when the branch was freshened, else the head the gate measured (verdict.pr.head_sha, or the batch item's head_sha). Before the squash, headRefOid is read up to six times, five seconds apart, through an injected sleep; a head GitHub never reports stops the round with drift and nothing is merged. A null expected head merges unpinned and says so with a progress line — reachable only when rev-parse returns nothing after a freshen. Batch tests' refresh fakes return no sha, so batch landings after the first are unpinned in those tests; the freshened-pin path is covered for a single round only.
